title: The perfect man keeps every feast at all times
source_text: Ἐὰν δέ τις πρὸς ταῦτα ἀνθυποφέρῃ τὰ περὶ τῶν παρ᾿ ἡμῖν κυριακῶν ἢ παρασκευῶν ἢ τοῦ Πάσχα ἢ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς δι᾿ ἡμερῶν γινόμενα, λεκτέον καὶ πρὸς τοῦτο ὅτι ὁ μὲν τέλειος, ἀεὶ ἐν τοῖς λόγοις ὢν καὶ τοῖς ἔργοις καὶ τοῖς διανοήμασι τοῦ τῇ φύσει κυρίου λόγου θεοῦ. ἀεί ἐστιν αὐτοῦ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις καὶ ἀεὶ ἄγει κυριακὰς ἡμέρας· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀεὶ παρασκευάζων ἑαυτὸν πρὸς τὸ ἀληθινῶς ζῆν καὶ ἀπεχόμενος τῶν τοῦ βίου ἡδέων καὶ τοὺς πολλοὺς ἀπατώντων καὶ μὴ τρέφων „τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς“ ἀλλ᾿ ὑπωπιάζων αὑτοῦ „τὸ σῶμα“ καὶ δουλαγωγῶν ἀεὶ ἄγει τὰς παρασκευάς. ἔτι δὲ ὁ νοήσας ὅτι „τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστὸς,“ καὶ χρὴ ἑορτάζειν ἐσθίοντα τῆς σαρκὸς τοῦ λόγου, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅτε οὐ ποιεῖ τὸ πάσχα, ὅπερ ἑρμηνεύεται διαβατήρια, διαβαίνων ἀεὶ τῷ λογισμῷ καὶ παντὶ λόγῳ καὶ πάσῃ πράξει ἀπὸ τῶν τοῦ βίου πραγμάτων ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτοῦ σπεύδων. πρὸς τούτοις δὲ ὁ δυνάμενος μετ᾿ ἀληθείας λέγειν· „συνανέστημεν τῷ Χριστῷ“ ἀλλὰ καὶ τό· „συνήγειρε καὶ συνεκάθισεν ἡμᾶς ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις ἐν Χριστῷ“ ἀεί ἐστιν ἐν ταῖς τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς ἡμέραις, καὶ μάλιστα ὅτε καὶ „εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον“ ὡς οἱ ἀπόστολοι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀναβὰς σχολάζει τῇ δεήσει καὶ „τῇ προσευχῇ,“ ὡς ἄξιος γενέσθαι τῆς „φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας“ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, βιαζομένης ἐξαφανίσαι τὴν ἐν ἀνθρώποις κακίαν καὶ τὰ ἀπ᾿ αὐτῆς, ἄξιος δὲ καί τινος μερισμοῦ γλώσσης ἀπὸ θεοῦ πυρίνης.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone counter-objects (ἀνθυποφέρῃ) to these things the matters of our Lord's days (κυριακαί), or Preparations (παρασκευαί), or the Pascha (πάσχα), or Pentecost (Πεντηκοστή) happening through days, it must be said also to this that the perfect one (τέλειος), being always in the words (λόγοι), works (ἔργα) and thoughts (διανοήματα) of the Word of God (λόγος θεοῦ), Lord by nature (τῇ φύσει κύριος), is always in His days and always keeps Lord's days. But also always preparing (παρασκευάζων) himself for truly living (ἀληθινῶς ζῆν), abstaining (ἀπεχόμενος) from the pleasures (ἡδέα) of life (βίος) which deceive (ἀπατώντων) the many, and not nourishing (τρέφων) 'the mind of the flesh', but beating (ὑπωπιάζων) his 'body' and enslaving it (δουλαγωγῶν), he always keeps the Preparations. Further, he who has understood (νοήσας) that 'our Pascha, Christ, was sacrificed (ἐτύθη)', and that one must keep festival (ἑορτάζειν) eating of the flesh (σάρξ) of the Word, there is no time he does not make the Pascha, which is interpreted crossing-sacrifices (διαβατήρια), always crossing (διαβαίνων) with reasoning (λογισμός) and every word and every deed (πρᾶξις) from the affairs of life to God, and hastening (σπεύδων) to His city (πόλις). Besides these, he who can say with truth: 'we rose together (συνανέστημεν) with Christ', and also 'He raised together (συνήγειρε) and seated together (συνεκάθισεν) us in the heavenlies (ἐπουράνια) in Christ', is always in the days of Pentecost, and most when, having gone up 'into the upper room (ὑπερῷον)' like the apostles of Jesus, he gives leisure (σχολάζει) to supplication (δέησις) and 'prayer (προσευχή)', so as to become worthy of 'the borne violent breath' from heaven, forcing (βιαζομένης) to make vanish (ἐξαφανίσαι) the wickedness (κακία) in men and what is from it, and worthy also of some distribution (μερισμός) of a fiery tongue (γλῶσσα πυρίνη) from God.
pass_b_english: If anyone objects to this by pointing to our own customs on set days, the Lord’s days, the days of Preparation, the Passover, or Pentecost, we must answer this too: the perfect man, who is always in the words, the works, and the thoughts of the Word of God, the One who is Lord by nature, is always in His days and always keeps the Lord’s days. Moreover, since he is always preparing himself for true life, abstaining from the pleasures of life that deceive the many, not feeding “the mind of the flesh” (Romans 8:6), but beating his “body” and bringing it into subjection (1 Corinthians 9:27), he always keeps the days of Preparation.

Further, he who has understood that “Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed” (1 Corinthians 5:7), and that we must keep the feast (1 Corinthians 5:8) by eating of the flesh of the Word (John 6:53), never fails to keep the Passover, which means the crossing-over. For he is always crossing over, in his reasoning and in every word and every action, from the affairs of this life to God, and hastening toward His city.

Besides this, he who can say with truth, “We have risen with Christ” (Colossians 3:1), and also, “He raised us up with Him and seated us with Him in the heavenly places in Christ” (Ephesians 2:6), is always in the days of Pentecost. This is above all so when, like the apostles of Jesus, he has gone up “into the upper room” (Acts 1:13) and gives himself to supplication and “prayer” (Acts 1:14), so as to become worthy of “the rushing of a mighty wind” from heaven (Acts 2:2), a wind that uses its might to wipe out the wickedness among men and all that comes from it, and worthy also of some share in a tongue of fire from God (Acts 2:3).

choices.choice: κυριακαί = ‘Lord’s days’ (Sundays); παρασκευαί = ‘days of Preparation’ (Fridays); kept as names so the wordplay on παρασκευάζων (‘preparing’) survives. τὰ περὶ τῶν παρ᾿ ἡμῖν ... δι᾿ ἡμερῶν γινόμενα is rendered ‘our own customs on set days’. πάσχα is rendered ‘Passover’ throughout, which keeps 1 Corinthians 5:7 in its usual English form and carries Origen’s gloss διαβατήρια (‘crossing-over’ feast). ‘The Word of God, the One who is Lord by nature’ renders τοῦ τῇ φύσει κυρίου λόγου θεοῦ; ‘His days’ (αὐτοῦ) is taken as the Word’s. ‘Christ, our Passover’ follows Origen’s word order τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός. ‘We have risen with Christ’ (συνανέστημεν τῷ Χριστῷ) is not an exact verse; nearest are Colossians 3:1 (συνηγέρθητε τῷ Χριστῷ) and Colossians 2:12; cited Colossians 3:1. Ephesians 2:6 quoted with ἐν Χριστῷ (without Ἰησοῦ). ‘Eating of the flesh of the Word’ is cited as an allusion to John 6:53; ‘keep the feast’ to 1 Corinthians 5:8 (ἑορτάζωμεν). ‘Hastening toward His city’ may echo Hebrews 11:16 or 12:22; left uncited as not certain. In Acts 2:2 Origen exploits βιαίας / βιαζομένης (‘mighty’ / ‘uses its might’). ‘Some share in a tongue of fire’ paraphrases Acts 2:3 (διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός).
Title: 'The Perfect Christian' to 'The Perfect Man' (Greek ὁ τέλειος; 'Christian' was an addition)

'pointing to what we do on set days, our Lord's days, our days of Preparation' to 'pointing to our own customs on set days, the Lord's days, the days of Preparation' ('our Lord's days' read as a possessive of Christ)
'of God's Word, who is by nature Lord' to 'of the Word of God, the One who is Lord by nature' (removes doubled 'who' clauses)
'And since he is always preparing' to 'Moreover, since he is always preparing' (ἀλλὰ καί)
'which is interpreted as the crossing-over' to 'which means the crossing-over' (calque of ἑρμηνεύεται)
All Scripture citations checked: Romans 8:6, 1 Corinthians 9:27, 5:7–8, John 6:53, Colossians 3:1, Ephesians 2:6, Acts 1:13–14, 2:2–3
